difficulty: a code listing with line numbers in a separate gutter column, and a shell transcript
title: Rotating Log Files
key_sentences: The script below rotates every log file in a folder and keeps a fixed number of old copies.
It was written for the quarry weighbridge, which writes a new log each day.
The transcript shows a run on the test machine.
Each log was moved to a copy ending in .1, and no new log had been written yet.
Run the script from the scheduler once a day, shortly after midnight.
code:
$ python rotate_logs.py /var/log/weighbridge
rotated 3 log files
$ ls /var/log/weighbridge
gate.log.1  scale.log.1  tickets.log.1
notes: code[0] is the Python listing WITHOUT its line numbers: the numbers 1-19 sit in a separate grey gutter column (its own pre element, right-aligned) and are not part of the code. Line 3 and line 15 are empty and still numbered. Indentation is spaces (4 per level). code[1] is the shell transcript in Courier New on a dark background, prompts '$ ' included; its last line separates names with two spaces.
